constructions.definition: Domain x_(2i-1)=x_(2i), i=1,...,m. Output parity of the m decoded bits.
constructions.proof_summary: There are no promised pairs at Hamming distance one, hence s=lambda=0. Substitution x_(2i-1)=x_(2i)=z_i converts any interpolating/approximating polynomial to parity on m bits, giving degree m. Flip whole pairs for bs=m. constructions.definition: Input (a,b) in {0,1}^{2m}. Domain: (|a|>=ceil(m/2), b=0^m) OR (a=0^m, |b|>=ceil(m/2)); output identifies the nonzero half.
constructions.proof_summary: Each promised input has a one-bit weak certificate: any of its 1 positions identifies the half. Sampling uniformly until a 1 is found is zero-error and uses at most four queries in expectation, so R0,R,Q,RC,bs are O(1). There are no opposite-output adjacent inputs. To lower-bound exact degree, symmetrize p(a,0) and p(0,b) separately. If degree is less than floor(m/2)+1, the first univariate polynomial is identically its required constant and the second is identically the other constant, because both agree at at least floor(m/2)+1 consecutive weights. Their values at zero must agree, a contradiction. Thus deg=Omega(m), QE>=deg/2, and D>=deg. Deterministic evaluation gives O(m) upper bounds.

constructions.definition: Input (a,b) in {0,1}^{2m}. Domain: a nonzero and b=0^m OR a=0^m and b nonzero. Output identifies the nonzero half.
constructions.proof_summary: Again C=RC=fbs=bs=1 and s=lambda=0. If p approximates the side label on the promise, amplify it on its two promised ranges to error 1/12 using a constant-degree polynomial. Then q(z)=p(0,z)-p(z,0), with sign chosen for the label convention, is zero at z=0 and within 1/6 of 1 for every nonzero z. It approximates total OR, so degree(p)=Omega(sqrt(m)). A bounded-error algorithm searches for a marked bit; the lower bound follows from this degree argument. Linear exact degree follows because the restrictions p(a,0) and p(0,b) would otherwise force incompatible values at their common origin.

constructions.definition: Domain consists of zero and the incidence vectors of lines in a projective plane of order t. Output distinguishes zero from a line. Use m=t as the growth parameter.

Recursive rows are indexed by a regular labelled tournament: each accepting clause requires strong predicates throughout its target row and weaker blocking predicates at labelled positions in outgoing rows. An OR of disjoint copies balances the two output sensitivities; disjoint self-composition amplifies the seed.
constructions.proof_summary: Random edge labels exclude excessive simultaneous near-satisfied clauses. Four coupled profiles control ordinary sensitivity and simultaneous flips of distinct nested predicates. Block witnesses at zero multiply through recursion; OR balancing gives s<=2(d+2)M^(d+1) and bs at zero >=M^2(2M^2+1)^d for M>=9^(d+1). Composition multiplies the zero-input block lower bound and at most multiplies sensitivity.

constructions.name: BKK and exact-checking cheat sheets
constructions.definition: Compose Block-k-sum gadgets to make a function with high quantum cost and cheap certificates. Its cheat-sheet totalization stores certificates at an address determined by several independent evaluations. The unique valid certificate cell controls certificate or polynomial degree.
constructions.proof_summary: BKK construction and cheat sheets. Apply a cheat sheet to a quantum-hard low-certificate function. The correct cheat-sheet cell is unique, so summing its exact checking polynomials gives small degree.

constructions.name: Recursive BKK cheat-sheet family

constructions.name: All-one-column pointer family
constructions.definition: A matrix has one marked all-one column. Pointers in that column encode a tree or chain of required zero entries elsewhere; the Boolean function accepts precisely valid marked structures. Parameters are balanced as in the cited source.
constructions.proof_summary: A unique all-one column carries pointers certifying zeros elsewhere. An adversary forces deterministic nm queries, while quantum search finds and verifies the candidate in O_tilde(sqrt(n)+sqrt(m)); take n=2m.

constructions.name: Randomized pointer and back-pointer family
constructions.definition: A pointer matrix hides the all-one column and its certificate. Random sampling and back pointers locate a valid certificate quickly, while an adaptive deterministic adversary delays discovery.
constructions.proof_summary: A pointer matrix has an adversarially hidden all-one column; random sampling and back pointers find its certificate quickly.

constructions.name: One-sided and zero-error pointer variant
constructions.definition: Modify the pointer and back-pointer verification to permit a cheap one-sided randomized or exact quantum algorithm. The zero-error randomized algorithm must still locate a full certificate.
constructions.proof_summary: A back-pointer variant makes one-sided randomized evaluation cheap while zero-error evaluation must locate a full certificate. Use exact quantum search in the same pointer construction with a zero-error randomized lower bound.

constructions.name: Several-marked-column pointer family
constructions.definition: Use the source variant with several marked columns. Exact quantum search and low-degree verification exploit the marked structure; planted distributions retain a large randomized query cost.
constructions.proof_summary: Several marked columns permit exact quantum search while planted distributions force many classical queries. Represent the pointer verification by low-degree polynomials while retaining the randomized lower bound.

constructions.name: Championship functions
constructions.definition: Encode competitions between candidates with race cards and verification information. Valid winners or virtual candidates can be found and checked by randomized or quantum tournament procedures; untouched cards force large negative certificates.
constructions.proof_summary: Sample race winners, eliminate candidates, verify; untouched cards force large 0-certificates. Virtual candidates, quantum tournament sink finding, and Grover verification.

constructions.name: Unambiguous-DNF cheat-sheet totalization F_n
constructions.definition: Start from the source unambiguous DNF, add position lists and count fields, and address a cheat-sheet cell containing the required checks. This is the same total family used for the joint certificate, quantum, exact and zero-error bounds.
constructions.proof_summary: DNF, position lists, cheat-sheet totalization, and source finding. Theorems 2.1 and 2.3 give Q<=O(sqrt(n)*log^3 n) and Q0=Theta(n*log^2 n). The zero-error lower bound restricts the count fields to AND on Theta(n*log^2 n) bits; a nonzero accepting amplitude for AND needs full degree. Exact term evaluation gives the matching Q0 upper bound. Together with C=Omega(n^2) and C=O(Q^4), logarithms of n and Q are comparable, yielding the quadratic lower exponent with polylog loss. Theorem 2.1 gives C>=Omega(n^2); Theorem 2.3 and Lemmas 7.3–7.4 give Q0=Theta(n*log^2 n). Thus C>=Omega(Q0^2/log^4 Q0). The count-field AND restriction forces the zero-error cost, and exact evaluation supplies its upper bound. Theorem 2.1 gives C>=Omega(n^2), while Theorem 2.3 gives QE=Theta(n*log^2 n). Hence C>=Omega(QE^2/log^4 QE). The exact algorithm finds the unambiguous terms, reads the selected bits and checks the addressed cheat-sheet cell; the AND restriction gives its lower bound. Use adeg<=2Q on the original AIK26 witness. If C<=O(adeg^p) held universally for p<4, the parameterized bounds would imply n^2<=O(n^(p/2) log(n)^(3p)), a contradiction. No conversion of log(n) into log(adeg) is needed. Certificate complexity lower bounds zero-error randomized complexity up to a constant. Apply this to the AIK26 witness, retaining its parameterized quantum upper bound.

constructions.name: Underlying AIK unambiguous DNF
constructions.definition: Use the unambiguous DNF before cheat-sheet totalization. The all-zero input has a large negative certificate because small zero restrictions still admit a positive completion; randomized elimination yields a cheap capped one-sided algorithm.
constructions.proof_summary: Unambiguous DNF with randomized elimination. One-sided algorithm is also two-sided. Lemma 3.4 ensures that any assignment of fewer than tau_n=n*(ceil(n/2)+1) variables consistent with all zeros still has a completion in the domain of H, hence a satisfying input of the underlying DNF. Therefore C0 at zero is Omega(n^2); input length gives the upper bound. The capped one-sided algorithm is Theorem 2.2.

constructions.name: Addressed outward-pointer cheat sheets

constructions.proof_summary: Addressed cheat sheets with outward pointers give a unique winner. A quantum tournament handles unreliable off-promise competitors; a planted hidden-zero argument and adaptive direct product force randomized address cost.

constructions.definition: Take a union of subcubes indexed by a doubly regular tournament. Each row imposes positive conditions and selected outgoing blocking coordinates. Label constraints limit the spectral norm, while many blocks change the all-zero input.

constructions.name: Balanced AND of ORs
constructions.definition: On an m by m Boolean matrix, take the AND over rows of their OR values. A zero row or one chosen one per row is a certificate; its exact polynomial contains the full-degree monomial.

constructions.name: forward multislice D unbounded domainDegree
constructions.definition: On permutations of [n], n even, use f(pi)=[the position of 1 is in the first half], with forward coordinate queries. A certificate is the single observed coordinate containing 1. These certificates partition both output classes, so C=UC=1. The sum of entry indicators for positions in the first half is an exact degree-one polynomial. Every sensitive change must include the original position of 1, so bs=fbs=s=1. An adversary avoids returning 1 for fewer than n/2 queries, leaving positions in both halves; querying a half suffices, hence D=n/2.

constructions.name: address unbounded nRelevant UC
constructions.definition: Use k address bits to select one of 2^k data bits. Every input bit is relevant, and reading the address followed by its selected data bit costs k+1. A deterministic tree supplies unambiguous certificate families from its leaves and simulates all the query measures here; fractional certificates and quantum verifiers cost at most the corresponding ordinary certificates/tree depth. Thus the right measure is at most O(k+1), while relevance is exponential in k. Total functions have a unique completion, so these witnesses lift unchanged.
